title: Danny Postma on building AI side projects fast and why distribution beats hype
summary: Danny Postma explains how he shipped several AI products in months (HeadshotPro, ProfilePicture AI, Deep Agency), what sells, and why a lone indie hacker needs distribution, SEO and stacked custom models rather than thin wrappers on a hyped model. He also covers how to start building and what to pick.

principles.text: Distribution and marketing matter more than building, especially in AI where wrappers have little moat.
principles.quote: you got to do distribution is everything marketing is everything it's really important it's always been important with product launches and especially with AI where you have less of a modes

principles.text: Don't build on a hype. Social attention fades, so aim for products that outlast it, using SEO and backlinks.
principles.quote: you shouldn't build on a hype so what I'm focusing on mostly now is SEO building tools getting backlinks um trying to get it to stand the time longer than just a hype

principles.text: Solve small, concrete problems and do the marketing; pick a problem that annoys you.
principles.quote: focus on like something small some small problems to solve and do your marketing to the distribution don't just build you got to sell it

principles.text: Build a moat by stacking many models into a custom pipeline rather than wrapping one model.
principles.quote: profile picture was just dream move it was there was no mode on it and what I'm doing with head Shield is basically it's 15 different AI models stacked on top of each other

principles.text: Target a clear paying use case, such as remote teams needing consistent headshots, and let users reveal new uses.
principles.quote: the head Shield has been the biggest success traffic wise Financial wise at the moment for remote teams

principles.text: Prices collapse when a big player enters, so launching early means you will be undercut.
principles.quote: lensa basically killed the whole market and after they went live right so yeah I think mostly now it's um it's the high quality output
